body: Created folders belong to a game installation, not to one package, so they are not added to each package's `directories` (exclusive folders only). Keeping `list --json` as an array avoids breaking consumers. `--download` is opt-in because a dry run must have no network or cache side effect unless the user asks; it validates that the cache is outside every game before downloading and is rejected without `--dry-run` or for standalone archives.
summary: The milestone 4 live run found that `list` hid the created-directory ledger and that catalog dry runs could not plan files for uncached `https` archives. Modn now prints the per-game created folders in `modn list` text and reports them as `created_directories` in `doctor --json`. `list --json` stays an array of packages. `install --dry-run --download` fetches missing `https` archives into the verified cache; a dry run still never downloads by default and never writes the game.
title: Created-folder ledger is reported by list text and doctor JSON; dry runs download only with --download

body: The old package's ownership stays recorded until the commit, so a failure or crash restores it under the same package ID and dependents keep valid links. The install path accepts exactly the update's uninstall journal as pending and excludes the old package from ownership, directory and conflict checks. The commit order matters because SQLite foreign keys are enforced: free the old file and directory rows first, insert the new package, then re-point package_dependencies and delete the old package row. Recovery must roll back the install journal first: otherwise restoring an old file meets the new file at the same path and recovery refuses. update_tests::recovery_restores_the_old_release_after_an_interrupted_update fails with the reversed order. Cleanup of a committed uninstall now refuses only when the live folder still has the old exclusive folder's identity, because the new release legitimately recreates that folder. The update preview hides the old release's paths from the read-only Lua host, so the policy plans as for a fresh install. Issue #48.
summary: Store::update_catalog_release withdraws the old release under a pending uninstall journal, installs the new release, and retires the old package in the new install's SQLite commit. Recovery rolls back pending installs before pending uninstalls.
title: A package update pairs a pending uninstall journal with a pending install journal

body: The layout is buckets/main/games/<game-id>/module.json and module.lua beside package manifests. Bootstrap downloads the running version release ZIP, verifies its built-in tree digest, validates it, and installs it atomically. MODN_MAIN_BUCKET_SOURCE permits an HTTPS URL or local ZIP without bypassing the digest. Explicit update downloads the latest release ZIP and SHA-256 sidecar over HTTPS, validates them and swaps atomically; failure preserves the prior copy. Registered local buckets reject module files and all buckets reject modules/ directories.
